message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate: 75 mph (often 70 mph).
• Urban interstate: 65 mph.
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for adults in Texas, but failure to buckle can lead to a fine if you’re pulled over. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (unless hands‑free).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | TxDOT – Mobile Phone Use | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is DUI.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield to emergency vehicles” applies to all vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal 100 ft before changing lanes.
• No “passing on the right” unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | TxDOT – Lane‑Changing Rules | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights only when visibility < 200 ft. | TxDOT – Headlight Regulations | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, crosswalks, or within 15 ft of a stop sign.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Registration must be renewed annually; proof displayed in the rear window.
• Minimum liability insurance required: $30,000/ $60,000 bodily injury per person, $25,000 bodily injury per accident, $25,000 property damage. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• No passing a stopped school bus until the bus’s stop sign is down and lights are off. | TxDOT – School Bus Regulations | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Speed cameras and red‑light cameras are used in many cities.
• Violations result in automatic tickets. | City of Austin, Dallas, Houston – Traffic Camera Policies | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial trucks must have a valid commercial driver’s license (CDL).
• Bicyclists must obey traffic signals and ride in the direction of traffic. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | --- ### How to Get Official, Up‑to‑Date Information 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary legal source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **TxDOT – Traffic Safety** – Offers fact sheets, statistics, and updates on enforcement. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html 3. **TxDMV – Driver Handbook** – Includes detailed rules, licensing requirements, and penalties. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/handbooks 4. **Local City Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas, Houston) have additional regulations, especially regarding parking, speed limits, and traffic cameras. *Example:* https://www.austintexas.gov/department/traffic-operations 5. **Legal Aid & Law Libraries** – For specific legal questions or case law references. *Example:* Texas State Law Library – https://www.tsl.state.tx.us/ --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your license, registration, and insurance documents in the vehicle.** - **Use hands‑free devices if you need to talk on the phone.** - **Check local speed limit signs; they can differ from state averages.** - **Be extra cautious in school zones and near construction sites.** - **If you’re pulled over, remain calm, keep your hands visible, and comply with the officer’s instructions.** Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent changes, or how to handle a particular traffic violation!
